title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR Tertio — Calvin nature vs judgment opener tip
pass_a_gloss: GAR opens Tertio: Calvin and the school set nature's force against divine judgment's reason as opposed explanations. He asks how Placeus can still call the corruption-spread God's just judgment when it runs so naturally that blocking it would mean fighting nature's order, overturning propagation laws, and choking off actual sin's natural follow-through. Tip into Placeus's Calvin reading.
pass_b_english: GAR. Third, since in this cause Calvin and the Theologians oppose these two—to be done by the force of nature, and to be done from the reason of divine judgment—how does the learned man say that is done by God's just judgment which is done so naturally that it cannot be hindered except against the order of nature, and unless the laws of natural propagation are overturned, and unless the sequel and natural efficacy of actual sin is stopped and checked?
source_text: GAR. Tertio cum in hac causa Calvinus & Theologi haec duo opponunt, fieri ex vi naturae, & fieri ex ratione judicii divini; quomodo vir doctus illud fieri dicit justo Dei judicio, quod fit ita naturaliter, ut impediri non possit, nisi contra naturae ordinem, & nisi evertantur leges naturalis propagationis, & nisi sistatur, & sufflaminetur peccati actualis sequela & efficacia naturalis?
